content: What happened to the older name that was so much descriptive?
@Patrick Massot What was the older name?
Why do you believe that would be a more appropriate name here?
We have to face up to the fact that the slop that LLMs were producing a year or so ago is not really representative of what the best ones can produce now.
I do sort of agree that the name could be a bit more descriptive of what the project actually is. Although I have no good suggestions for what it could be. All I can think of is Mecha-Mathlib :joy:
Anything that has "mathlib" or another hand-curated project in its name is not the correct branding for this and similar projects.
btw merely-true was a good name IMO (though some people found it offensive)
merely-true was a good name for something else: I'm not sure if people realise we actually created it: https://github.com/merely-true/merely-true

Tau Ceti is doing many things beyond "merely true":

  • all content is adversarially reviewed against open rubrics
  • new content must be preceded by a reviewed, informal roadmap
  • infrastructure and inference to keep bumping toolchains and the Mathlib dependency, and to refactor as needed to always reuse Mathlib as much as possible
  • extra tooling such as radar, the PR topic, and docgen
  • some social infrastructure, e.g.
    • this channel,
    • plans to integrate with project-intentions, auditing projects, and search tools,
    • coordination and communication with relevant mathlib teams, the Mathlib Initiative, the Lean FRO, AI companies, and academia (e.g. I'm going to talk about Tau Ceti at a National Academy of Sciences meeting tomorrow!)
    • at the right time, a steering committee for Tau Ceti
Just curious, is the name "Tau Ceti" coming form anything?
And why the symbol of octopus? Because people in zulip use it for no reason?
That's the Lean Hexapus, I think it is our mascot. Like the rust crab... but if it was a mollusc

Felix Pernegger said:

Just curious, is the name "Tau Ceti" coming form anything?

As the links above say, it's a nearby star (indeed, one of the closer "sun like" stars to our own). It's the site of countless sci-fi stories about visiting nearby stars.

(In fact, Hail Mary is set there, although I'd forgotten that when I picked the name and was thinking of older ones.)

Personally I like the name for both its astronomical connotations (it's nearby and not entirely alien, yet still very far away), and for the sci-fi connotations (let's try something a bit ambitious and experimental).

Kevin Buzzard said:

We have to face up to the fact that the slop that LLMs were producing a year or so ago is not really representative of what the best ones can produce now.

:100:
And it's crazy to think that it's just the beginning

Regarding the thread itself, it may be a popular opinion that a more descriptive name would be a better fit

From wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stars_in_fiction#Tau_Ceti):

The Tau Ceti system is a common setting in science fiction. James Nicoll, writing for Tor.com, attributes this to a confluence of factors that make it the nearest star (at a distance of approximately 12 light-years) that could plausibly harbour habitable planets, including having a favourable brightness and being a solitary rather than multiple star. In 2015, Andrew Liptak interviewed several authors about why they used Tau Ceti for their stories; in addition to the star's relative proximity to Earth, Ursula K. Le Guin (who wrote The Dispossessed, 1974) and Larry Niven (The Legacy of Heorot, 1987, with Jerry Pournelle and Steven Barnes) cited the star's similarity to the Sun, while Kim Stanley Robinson (Aurora, 2015) pointed to the recent discovery of several exoplanets around Tau Ceti.

There is also this wikipedia category of "Fiction set around Tau Ceti"

One cautionary tale (narrated by the ship's AI) is Aurora where the planet turns out to be inhospitable.
(Perhaps no surprise to admit that I have read all the above, and Aurora in particular is a book I enjoyed very much. It's nice to feel the sand between your toes after a long time away.)
